doc.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016

title: Closing thanks and the evening's gig
summary: Jenkins thanks the archive, explains how tonight's tunes were chosen, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well is there anything that I haven’t asked you that you’d like to offer?

I’m just honored to be here and thankful for people like you that care enough about this stuff — because I’m not a huge name and I’m just humbled by all these pictures and the fact that you are doing this. It’s amazing to me. And you’re studied and you’re prepared and you’re respectful. We all so appreciate people like you.
Well thanks. On the gig tonight, do you get to call the tunes?

Well I sent several of the things I do, some of them are obscure Bird and Monk tunes. And Mike Dubaniewicz, who was a student of ours at Eastman, and I sent him a few of my originals and he was great. He rehearsed the band and he set up two sets for tonight and he kind of picked out of the stuff I sent. Because I left it up to him because he knows his guys and then we’re going to do a couple of arrangements of his. So indirectly yes, but I left it up to him for what he would be comfortable with. I sent some stuff that was not very hard, and he set up two great sets. So I think it will be a lot of fun.
Yeah. It should be. Well thanks for your time today.
